" SVP, Fortune 100 Home Improvement Retailer Computer Vision in Retail FAQs What is computer vision in retail? Computer vision in retail is the use of sensors and AI to interpret images of store shelves, products, and pricing in real time. Computer vision enables retailers to detect out-of-stocks, pricing errors, and planogram gaps automatically, replacing manual audits with continuous, accurate data. Simbe's Tally shelf-scanning robot and Tally spot fixed sensors use computer vision to scan aisles multiple times per day, giving associates a live view of shelf conditions and prioritized actions to resolve them. How do retailers reduce out-of-stocks with technology? Retailers reduce out-of-stocks by replacing periodic manual shelf checks with continuous autonomous monitoring that detects gaps in real time. Autonomous shelf-scanning robots like Tally, and fixed sensors like Tally Spot, capture shelf conditions multiple times per day, flag low-stock and missing items, and deliver prioritized restocking alerts directly to store teams. Wakefern Food Corp. improved on-shelf availability by 50% across more than 90 stores using Simbe's Store Intelligence platform. What is a store intelligence platform? A store intelligence platform unifies real-time data from physical stores, including shelf conditions, inventory levels, pricing, and planogram compliance, into a single source of actionable truth. Unlike point solutions, a store intelligence platform combines multiple data streams from autonomous robots, fixed sensors, and existing retailer systems. Simbe pioneered the category and operates the only vertically integrated platform purpose-built for retail. What ROI do retailers see from inventory automation? Retailers using autonomous inventory automation typically see measurable gains in on-shelf availability, pricing accuracy, and reallocated hours within the first 60 to 120 days. Simbe has driven significant results for retailers such as BJ's Wholesale Club, Schnuck Markets, and SPAR Austria, including up to 60% improvement in on-shelf availability, 70% improvement in price accuracy, and 50 hours per week rededicated to shoppers. Simbe's robot-as-a-service (RaaS) model lowers upfront cost by bundling hardware, software, and support into a subscription. What makes an inventory robot effective in a retail store? Effective inventory robots combine full-store coverage, multiple daily scans, and accurate shelf-level data delivered fast enough for store teams to act on. Multimodal coverage—including mobile robots paired with fixed sensors and RFID—captures every zone, including upper steel, apparel, and recessed shelves that other capture options miss. Simbe's Tally navigates 150K square-foot stores and localizes within 1 to 2 inches, operating during business hours without disrupting shoppers or store associates. What are out-of-stocks costing your stores? Even small gaps on the shelf add up to significant lost revenue. Estimate the business impact for your stores in minutes.
